questions.question:
Este es el prompt (en inglés) que usaré para generar la especificación. ¿Lo apruebas?

---
Feature: Pause and resume a listing without losing its ranking.

WHY: Sellers on the marketplace sometimes need to take a listing off sale temporarily (out of stock, on vacation) without deleting it, and without losing the ranking it has earned from past orders. When they bring it back, it should regain its place in search exactly as before.

WHAT:
- Add two actions to the listings API: `POST /listings/:id/pause` and `POST /listings/:id/resume`. A paused listing has status `paused`; a resumed listing goes back to status `active`.
- Pausing and resuming never change the listing's ranking score.
- Who may pause/resume: the seller who owns the listing, and admins. A pause made by an admin can be resumed by the owning seller or by an admin — a pause is the same whoever made it.
- While paused, the listing is hidden from search (`GET /listings`) for everyone. After resume it reappears in its position according to its unchanged ranking.
- While paused, `GET /listings/:id` still returns the listing to anyone, showing status `paused`.
- While paused, ordering the listing (`POST /listings/:id/orders`) is rejected: no order is created and the ranking does not change. Orders that already existed before the pause are not affected in any way.
- Repeated actions are idempotent: pausing an already-paused listing or resuming an already-active listing succeeds and changes nothing.
- Rejected pause/resume requests follow the API's existing error conventions: no user or unknown user -> 401 `unauthenticated`; a user without permission (another seller, a buyer) -> 403 (exact error text left to the implementation); unknown listing -> 404 `listing_not_found`.
- The exact success response of pause/resume (status code and body) is left to the implementation by the user's decision.

References: none beyond the existing listings API in this repository (current behavior: search returns all listings sorted by ranking; ordering does not check status; each order adds 1 ranking point).

Non-goals: pause history or audit of who paused; remembering who paused; scheduled or auto-expiring pauses; any change to how ranking is calculated.

Open decisions (Do not resolve these; mark each `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`):
- The error status code and error text returned when someone tries to order a paused listing (candidates discussed: 409 `listing_paused`, 404 `listing_not_found`, 422 `listing_paused`).
---

2) Punto de búsqueda: "While paused, the listing is hidden from search (`GET /listings`) for everyone. After resume it reappears in search, ranked by its preserved score using the normal search ordering; its position is not guaranteed to be the one it had before the pause, since other listings may have overtaken it."

Este es el borrador completo del objetivo (goal.md), en inglés como el código. ¿Lo apruebas?

# Goal — pause and resume a listing

## Goal condition
`npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` all exit 0, and the test suite contains passing tests that exercise every acceptance criterion below through the HTTP API (e.g. after `POST /listings/l_chair/pause` as `u_seller_ana`, `GET /listings/l_chair` returns `status: "paused"` with `rankScore` 30, `GET /listings` no longer contains `l_chair`, and after `POST /listings/l_chair/resume` it is back first in `GET /listings`).

## Acceptance criteria
- AC-1 `POST /listings/:id/pause` by the listing's owning seller, or by any admin, sets the listing's `status` to `paused` and answers 200 with the updated listing.
- AC-2 `POST /listings/:id/resume` by the owning seller, or by any admin, sets `status` back to `active` and answers 200 with the updated listing.
- AC-3 Pausing and resuming never change `rankScore` (nor any other field besides `status`).
- AC-4 Pausing an already-paused listing, or resuming an already-active listing, answers 200 with the listing unchanged.
- AC-5 `GET /listings` (search) excludes paused listings for every caller; once resumed, the listing reappears in the position its unchanged `rankScore` gives it.
- AC-6 `GET /listings/:id` returns a paused listing to any caller, showing `status: "paused"`.
- AC-7 `POST /listings/:id/orders` on a paused listing is rejected with an error response (4xx, body `{ "error": <code> }`); no order is created and `rankScore` does not change. The exact status and error code are the implementer's choice (delegated by the user) and must be reported.
- AC-8 Orders that already existed on a listing before it was paused are unchanged and still listed by `GET /orders` as today.
- AC-9 Pause/resume caller errors follow the existing route conventions: no or unknown `x-user-id` → 401 `unauthenticated`; unknown listing → 404 `listing_not_found`; a caller who is neither the owning seller nor an admin → 403 `not_listing_owner`.

## Constraints
- All existing tests keep passing unchanged; existing endpoints behave as today for active listings.
- `ListingStatus` gains `paused`; no other data-model change. The ranking formula is not changed.
- Error bodies keep the `{ "error": <code> }` shape; caller identity keeps coming from `x-user-id`.

## Out of scope
Editing or deleting listings, scheduled/automatic pauses, pause history or timestamps, changes to how ranking is computed, cancelling or modifying existing orders.

## References
None beyond this codebase's existing conventions.

options.label: Aprobar
options.description: Usar este goal.md tal cual.

options.description: Indica los cambios en 'Other'.

answers.Este es el borrador completo del objetiv: Editar: AC-5 dice que la búsqueda reapareció "en la posición que su rankScore no modificado le da", pero la verdad (P4) establece que "su posición de búsqueda no está garantizada — otros anuncios pueden haberla superado entre tanto". Mientras el rankScore se preserva exactamente, otros anuncios pueden haber cambiado de ranking, por lo que la posición final no es determinística. AC-5 debería reconocer que la posición en resultados depende de cómo rankea respecto a otros anuncios en ese momento, no garantizar que vuelve a su posición anterior.

Goal condition: `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` all exit 0, and the test suite contains passing tests that exercise every acceptance criterion below through the HTTP API (e.g. after `POST /listings/l_chair/pause` as `u_seller_ana`, `GET /listings/l_chair` returns `status: "paused"` with `rankScore` 30 and `GET /listings` no longer contains `l_chair`; after `POST /listings/l_chair/resume`, `l_chair` is back in `GET /listings` with `rankScore` 30, sorted against the other listings by their current scores).

AC-5 `GET /listings` (search) excludes paused listings for every caller. Once resumed, the listing appears in search again with its `rankScore` exactly as before the pause; its position is whatever that score gives it against the other listings at that moment — it is not guaranteed to return to its previous position, since other listings may have overtaken it meanwhile.
